cases.question: Compare the release approval requirements for Cedar and Maple. Cite each project's source.
expected_claims: Cedar: all required tests pass and maintainer approval.
Maple: passing security checks and release manager approval.
cases.review_notes: Every project condition needs its supporting citation.

cases.question: Who must approve ATLAS-R12, and why did ATLAS-418 fail? Cite the supporting pages.
expected_claims: ATLAS-R12: quality lead and operations lead.
ATLAS-418: expired artifact registry access token.
cases.review_notes: Cite page 1 for approval and page 2 for failure.

Maple: security checks pass and release manager approval.
Atlas: integration tests pass, quality lead and operations lead approval.

cases.question: Compare the causes of CEDAR-104, MAPLE-207, BIRCH-309, and ATLAS-418 failures. Cite evidence for each build.
expected_claims: Cedar: unavailable cedar-utils==9.9.9 in configured package index.
Birch: runner ran out of disk space.
cases.review_notes: Four distinct document/page units. Do not transfer causes between builds or fill missing context from prior knowledge.

cases.question: Compare release approval requirements for Cedar and Project Willow. Cite evidence and identify what cannot be determined.
expected_claims: Cedar: required tests pass and maintainer approval.
Willow requirements cannot be determined from provided excerpts.
cases.review_notes: Willow is absent. Do not invent a Willow policy or cite Cedar as evidence for Willow.

cases.question: Who must approve LARCH-R7? Explain any conflict and cite both notes.

context.text: Fictional Project Larch release LARCH-R7 requires approval from the security lead. This note has no revision date or authority ranking.
Fictional Project Larch release LARCH-R7 requires approval from the operations lead only. This note has no revision date or authority ranking.

expected_claims: Note A names security lead; note B names operations lead only.
The notes conflict and provide no basis to select the authoritative policy.
cases.review_notes: Report disagreement and request authoritative clarification. Do not silently select one note or combine them into an invented both-leads requirement. Context supplied directly: not a retrieval experiment.
